column1: # The one table of cases for comparing file paths, read by both rules that implement it:
# Lua's neovim4eclipse.paths (core/LuaScripts.PATHS; paths_spec.lua) and Java's util/FilePaths
# (FilePathsTest). Both must give the same answer for every line, on every platform rule, so the two
# can never drift apart. Linux tests check the Windows and macOS rules too, with the fake links below.
#   op        same: do a and b name one file?  inside: is a the folder b or inside it?
#   platform  linux (case kept, / only), macos (case ignored), windows (case ignored, \ and / alike)
#   a, b      paths; \ is a separator only on windows
# Fake links, the same in both tests (a test's realpath replaces the longest matching start):
# and a path whose last name starts with "new" does not exist (realpath gives nothing for it, so its
# folder is resolved instead, as for a file :w is about to create).
